title: What a data engineer does and how it differs from a data scientist

videos.script: Monday morning at a bicycle-sharing company, and the operations manager asks a simple question. Which stations ran out of bicycles last week, and for how long? {{question}} Nobody can answer it yet, because the answer is spread over three systems. An app database, a sensor in every dock, and a spreadsheet the mechanics keep. {{three-systems}} Somebody has to copy all three out every day, without losing a single file. Then put them on one clock, and check every morning that yesterday arrived. {{the-work}} That somebody is a data engineer, and when the work goes well nobody sees it. {{invisible}} This lesson is about that job, and how it differs from the two beside it. The data scientist predicts what will happen, and the analyst answers what did. {{roles}} Then you build the lab the whole course runs on: one directory, one Python, two libraries. {{lab}} And you run a first program, with six rides, one question and two ways to break it. One of them stops with an error that names the problem. The other quietly counts a ride twice, and the output still looks right. {{two-failures}} That second kind of failure is what the rest of this course is about. {{end}}
